blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: Pharaoh, the king of Egypt, was afraid of the Hebrew people because there were getting to be so many of them. So he gave a cruel order. Every Hebrew baby boy was to be thrown into the river. The girls could live.

verses.text: And there went a man of the house of Levi, and took to wife a daughter of Levi.

verses.text: And the woman conceived, and bare a son: and when she saw him that he was a goodly child, she hid him three months.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And the woman conceived, and bare a son: and when she saw him that he was a goodly child, she hid him three months.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: A goodly child. That mother looked at her baby boy and could not give him up. Three months she hid him. Imagine trying to keep a newborn quiet, Church, when every cry could get him killed.

verses.text: And when she could not longer hide him, she took for him an ark of bulrushes, and daubed it with slime and with pitch, and put the child therein; and she laid it in the flags by the river’s brink.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: When she could not hide him anymore, she made a little ark out of bulrushes. She sealed it with slime and pitch so it would float. She laid her baby inside and set it down in the reeds by the river. The same river Pharaoh meant for death, she trusted to carry life.

verses.text: And his sister stood afar off, to wit what would be done to him.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And his sister stood afar off, to wit what would be done to him.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: His big sister stood watching from a ways off. She did not leave him. She wanted to know what would happen to her little brother.

verses.text: And the daughter of Pharaoh came down to wash herself at the river; and her maidens walked along by the river’s side; and when she saw the ark among the flags, she sent her maid to fetch it.

verses.text: And when she had opened it, she saw the child: and, behold, the babe wept. And she had compassion on him, and said, This is one of the Hebrews’ children.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: The baby was crying, and the daughter of Pharaoh had compassion on him. She knew he was a Hebrew child, one of the very babies her father ordered killed. She chose mercy anyway.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: Then that sister stepped up. Think how brave that was, a young Hebrew girl speaking up to the daughter of Pharaoh.

verses.text: Then said his sister to Pharaoh’s daughter, Shall I go and call to thee a nurse of the Hebrew women, that she may nurse the child for thee?

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: The sister ran and got her own mother, the baby's mother.

verses.text: And Pharaoh’s daughter said unto her, Take this child away, and nurse it for me, and I will give thee thy wages. And the woman took the child, and nursed it.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: Say it with me. Somebody say, look at God. [PAUSE 3s | screen: "Look at God"] Look at God. [PAUSE 3s | screen: "Look at God"] That mother got her baby back, and got paid to nurse him.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: The mother who hid her son and set him in that river was handed him right back. She would nurse him, and she would get paid for it. Her baby was safe in her arms again.

verses.text: And the child grew, and she brought him unto Pharaoh’s daughter, and he became her son. And she called his name Moses: and she said, Because I drew him out of the water.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: The boy grew. When he was older, his mother brought him to Pharaoh's daughter, and he became her son. She named him Moses, because she drew him out of the water.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: This story turns on some women. A mother who would not give up her son. A sister who watched and spoke up. A princess who chose compassion over her daddy's order. Through them, God kept the child who would one day lead his people out of Egypt.
